name: AECi — Auth sign-in error rate > 30% (15m)
message:
More than 30% of sign-in completions failed over 15m (AECI-206 / Phase 5.15). `aeci.auth.signin` is emitted by the SSR Worker (service:aeci-web) at /auth/callback — one per completion, `outcome:success|failed` with a failure `reason` (`link_invalid` / `missing_code` / `auth_not_configured`). A spike usually means a broken redirect/callback config, an expired/misconfigured Supabase project, or a provider (Google OAuth) outage — NOT necessarily user error. Pivot the 'AECi Phase 5 — Auth/Reviews' dashboard by `method` (google/magic_link) and `reason` to localize it, and read `service:aeci-web` logs at /auth/callback.

Note: 'attempts' here are sign-in *completions* reaching the callback; browser-side initiation (magic-link send / OAuth start) is a deferred RUM signal (docs/OBSERVABILITY.md), so a user who never returns isn't counted. This monitor deliberately does NOT use notify_no_data — sign-ins are traffic-driven, so zero completions (no logins) is normal at pre-launch and a no-data alert would fire constantly. The 30% threshold is a launch-tunable starting point — at low pre-launch volume a single failed completion can dominate the ratio; retune once production traffic is known.

Runbook: https://github.com/the-wbs-project/aec-integrations/blob/main/docs/RUNBOOKS.md#auth-sign-in-error-rate-spike
